entries.pick: you want the most polished experience, best mobile/TV apps, and don't mind vendor lock-in + cloud account requirement.

alternatives.name: Jellyfin
alternatives.text: Plex if you want polish and broad device support; Jellyfin if you want no account, no paywall, fully open.

entries.name: Navidrome
prose: Lightweight music server compatible with Subsonic/Airsonic clients. Scans your music library, provides a web UI and API for streaming.
entries.pick: you only need music (not video) and want something extremely lightweight with Subsonic API compatibility.

alternatives.name: Jellyfin
alternatives.text: Navidrome if you only need music and want minimal footprint; Jellyfin if you want one server for all media types.

categories.label: Monitoring
categories.description: Uptime monitoring, metrics, alerting, and observability

entries.name: Uptime Kuma
prose: Self-hosted monitoring tool with a beautiful UI. HTTP/TCP/DNS/ping/push monitors, status pages, notifications via 90+ channels (Slack, Discord, Telegram, etc.).
entries.pick: you want simple uptime monitoring with a gorgeous UI, easy setup, and zero config files.

alternatives.name: Grafana + Prometheus
alternatives.text: Uptime Kuma for uptime/status page monitoring; Grafana+Prometheus for full metrics/observability.

entries.name: Grafana
prose: The industry-standard dashboarding and visualization platform. Connects to dozens of data sources (Prometheus, Loki, InfluxDB, PostgreSQL, etc.).
entries.pick: you want beautiful, customizable dashboards for metrics, logs, and traces from multiple sources.

alternatives.name: Uptime Kuma
alternatives.text: Different tools. Grafana visualizes metrics; Uptime Kuma monitors uptime. Often used together.

entries.name: Prometheus
prose: Pull-based metrics collection and time-series database. The backbone of most self-hosted observability stacks. Pairs with Grafana for visualization and Alertmanager for notifications.
entries.pick: you want a proper metrics pipeline with alerting rules and long-term storage.

alternatives.name: Uptime Kuma
alternatives.text: Prometheus for full observability (CPU, memory, custom app metrics); Uptime Kuma for simple "is it up?" checks.

categories.label: Networking
categories.description: Reverse proxies, DNS, VPNs, tunnels, and network management

entries.name: Nginx Proxy Manager
prose: GUI for managing Nginx reverse proxy with Let's Encrypt SSL, access lists, and stream proxying. Point-and-click SSL cert management.
entries.pick: you want dead-simple reverse proxy management with a GUI and don't want to write config files.

alternatives.name: Traefik
alternatives.text: NPM for GUI-first management; Traefik for Docker-native auto-discovery and config-as-code.

alternatives.name: Caddy
alternatives.text: NPM for GUI; Caddy for minimal config files with automatic HTTPS.

entries.name: Traefik

fields.Auth: none built-in (use middleware or external auth)

prose: Cloud-native reverse proxy that auto-discovers services from Docker, Kubernetes, and other providers. Config-as-code via labels.
entries.pick: you want auto-discovery of Docker containers, dynamic config via labels, and a dashboard for monitoring routes.

alternatives.name: NPM
alternatives.text: Traefik for automation and Docker-native workflows; NPM for GUI simplicity.

alternatives.name: Caddy
alternatives.text: Traefik for Docker/K8s auto-discovery; Caddy for simplicity and the cleanest config format.

entries.name: Pi-hole
prose: Network-wide DNS sinkhole for ad blocking. Also functions as a DHCP server and local DNS resolver (great for split-horizon setups).
entries.pick: you want network-level ad blocking and local DNS management with a mature, well-documented project.

alternatives.name: AdGuard Home
alternatives.text: Pi-hole for maturity and community size; AdGuard Home for modern UI, DoH/DoT built-in, and per-client settings.

entries.name: AdGuard Home
prose: DNS-level ad blocking with DNS-over-HTTPS, DNS-over-TLS, and per-client filtering rules built in. More modern UI than Pi-hole.
entries.pick: you want encrypted DNS (DoH/DoT) out of the box, per-client rules, and a cleaner UI.

alternatives.name: Pi-hole
alternatives.text: AdGuard Home for modern features and encrypted DNS; Pi-hole for larger community, more guides, and longer track record.

categories.label: Notes & Wikis
categories.description: Note-taking apps, personal knowledge management, and wiki software

entries.name: SilverBullet
prose: An open-source, self-hosted personal knowledge management platform built on plain Markdown files. Runs entirely in the browser as a PWA with offline support, backed by a Deno server. Features wiki-style bi-directional linking, a built-in query language, live-preview editing, and a Lua scripting environment for programmable note-taking. Your notes are just files on disk — fully compatible with Obsidian vaults and any Markdown editor.
entries.pick: you want an Obsidian-like experience that's self-hosted, works in the browser, keeps notes as plain Markdown files, and you value extensibility through scripting over a locked-in app.

alternatives.name: Joplin Server
alternatives.text: SilverBullet is browser-native with plain files on disk; Joplin uses dedicated desktop/mobile clients with encrypted sync to a server. Choose SilverBullet for hackability and file portability; Joplin for cross-device encrypted sync with native apps.

alternatives.name: Memos
alternatives.text: SilverBullet is a full PKM system (wiki linking, queries, pages); Memos is a quick-capture microblog. SilverBullet for structured knowledge; Memos for fleeting thoughts.

alternatives.name: Wiki.js
alternatives.text: SilverBullet is personal-first with local Markdown files and scripting. Wiki.js is team-facing with a database backend, WYSIWYG editor, and access controls for organizational wikis.

alternatives.name: HedgeDoc
alternatives.text: SilverBullet is for personal knowledge management; HedgeDoc is for real-time collaborative document editing. Different use cases — choose SilverBullet for your second brain, HedgeDoc for team writing sessions.

entries.name: Joplin Server

fields.License: Joplin Server Personal Use License (non-commercial; clients are AGPL-3.0)

prose: Self-hosted sync server for the Joplin note-taking ecosystem. Joplin clients (desktop, mobile, CLI) support end-to-end encryption, Markdown editing, notebooks, tags, and to-do lists. The server enables fast sync between devices, note sharing via public URLs, and notebook sharing between users. Also supports sync via WebDAV, Nextcloud, Dropbox, or OneDrive without the dedicated server.
entries.pick: you want encrypted cross-device note sync with native desktop and mobile apps, and you value end-to-end encryption and an Evernote-like experience with import support.

alternatives.name: SilverBullet
alternatives.text: Joplin has polished native clients and E2EE; SilverBullet is browser-only but offers programmability and plain Markdown files. Joplin for mobile-first encrypted notes; SilverBullet for hackable PKM.

alternatives.name: Memos
alternatives.text: Joplin is a full notebook system with encryption, attachments, and rich organization. Memos is minimalist quick-capture. Joplin if you need structured notes across devices; Memos for rapid jotting.

alternatives.name: Wiki.js
alternatives.text: Joplin is personal note-taking with sync; Wiki.js is a team wiki with web UI, search, and access control. Different audiences entirely.

alternatives.name: HedgeDoc
alternatives.text: Joplin is for personal encrypted notes synced across devices; HedgeDoc is for real-time collaborative editing in a browser. Joplin for private notes; HedgeDoc for team collaboration.

entries.name: Memos
prose: A lightweight, open-source, self-hosted note-taking and microblog app designed for quick capture. Twitter-like timeline for jotting thoughts, with Markdown support, tags, pinning, sharing, and a web clipper. Single Go binary with minimal resource usage — deploys in seconds. Supports REST and gRPC APIs for integration.
entries.pick: you want a dead-simple, low-resource place to quickly capture thoughts, snippets, and links — like a private Twitter/microblog for your ideas.

alternatives.name: SilverBullet
alternatives.text: Memos is for fast, unstructured capture (tweets/fleeting notes); SilverBullet is for building a structured knowledge base with linking and queries. Memos for speed; SilverBullet for depth.

alternatives.name: Joplin Server
alternatives.text: Memos is a lightweight single-app experience in the browser; Joplin is a full notebook ecosystem with native clients and encryption. Memos for casual quick notes; Joplin for serious cross-device note management.

alternatives.name: Wiki.js
alternatives.text: Memos is personal and ephemeral; Wiki.js is structured, team-oriented documentation. Completely different purposes — Memos won't replace a wiki.

alternatives.name: HedgeDoc
alternatives.text: Memos is solo quick-capture; HedgeDoc is collaborative long-form editing. Memos for personal micro-notes; HedgeDoc for writing documents together.

entries.name: Wiki.js

fields.Auth: built-in, OIDC, LDAP, SAML, OAuth (30+ providers)

prose: A powerful, modern wiki engine built on Node.js with a beautiful interface. Features a WYSIWYG and Markdown editor, full-text search (Elasticsearch/PostgreSQL), granular permissions, page versioning, comments, diagrams, and built-in diagramming (Mermaid, PlantUML). Supports 30+ authentication strategies and multiple storage backends (git, S3, local). Excellent for team documentation and knowledge bases.
entries.pick: you need a proper team wiki with fine-grained access control, search, versioning, and a polished web interface — a Confluence/Notion alternative for documentation.

alternatives.name: SilverBullet
alternatives.text: Wiki.js is team-facing with structured permissions, search, and a database backend. SilverBullet is personal-first with plain files and scripting. Wiki.js for organizational docs; SilverBullet for personal PKM.

alternatives.name: Joplin Server
alternatives.text: Wiki.js is a web-first wiki for teams; Joplin is personal note sync with native apps. Different tools for different problems.

alternatives.name: Memos
alternatives.text: Wiki.js is structured documentation; Memos is quick-capture snippets. Wiki.js when you need organized, searchable, permission-controlled content.

alternatives.name: HedgeDoc
alternatives.text: Wiki.js is a permanent, structured wiki with versioning and permissions. HedgeDoc is for real-time collaborative editing of individual documents. Wiki.js for your knowledge base; HedgeDoc for live co-authoring sessions.

entries.name: HedgeDoc

fields.Auth: built-in, OIDC, LDAP, SAML, OAuth (GitHub, Google, etc.)

prose: An open-source, real-time collaborative Markdown editor (formerly CodiMD). Multiple users edit the same document simultaneously with visible cursors, live preview, and conflict-free merging. Supports slides (reveal.js), diagrams (Mermaid, PlantUML), math (MathJax), tables, and embeds. Great for meeting notes, documentation drafts, and collaborative writing.
entries.pick: you need Google Docs-style real-time collaboration on Markdown documents — meeting notes, design docs, or any content multiple people write together.

alternatives.name: SilverBullet
alternatives.text: HedgeDoc is multi-user real-time collaboration on single documents; SilverBullet is personal knowledge management. HedgeDoc for team writing; SilverBullet for your second brain.

alternatives.name: Joplin Server
alternatives.text: HedgeDoc is collaborative web editing; Joplin is personal encrypted sync. HedgeDoc for shared documents; Joplin for private cross-device notes.

alternatives.name: Memos
alternatives.text: HedgeDoc is for longer collaborative documents; Memos is solo quick-capture. Entirely different use cases.

alternatives.name: Wiki.js
alternatives.text: HedgeDoc excels at real-time co-authoring of individual documents. Wiki.js is a structured wiki with hierarchy, permissions, and search. Use HedgeDoc for live collaboration; Wiki.js for your permanent knowledge base.

categories.label: Photos
categories.description: Photo and video management, backup, and sharing

entries.name: Immich
prose: Google Photos alternative with mobile auto-backup, facial recognition, map view, shared albums, and ML-powered search. Excellent mobile apps (iOS/Android).
> **Note:** Immich is under very active development. Breaking changes between versions are common. Check release notes before upgrading.
entries.pick: you want the closest experience to Google Photos with auto-backup from phone, face detection, and ML search.

alternatives.name: PhotoPrism
alternatives.text: Immich for mobile-first auto-backup workflow; PhotoPrism for existing photo libraries and DAM-style browsing.

entries.name: PhotoPrism
prose: AI-powered photo management that indexes your existing library. Face/object detection, map views, albums. More focused on browsing/organizing than mobile backup.
entries.pick: you have an existing photo library on disk and want to browse it with AI-powered search without moving files around.

alternatives.name: Immich
alternatives.text: PhotoPrism for organizing existing libraries; Immich for phone-to-server auto-backup workflow.

categories.label: Recipes
categories.description: Recipe management, meal planning, and shopping lists

entries.name: Mealie
prose: Self-hosted recipe manager with integrated meal planning, shopping lists, and cookbooks. Import recipes by URL with automatic scraping. REST API for third-party integrations. Vue frontend, Python/FastAPI backend, SQLite or PostgreSQL.
entries.pick: you want the most polished all-in-one experience with meal planning, shopping lists, URL import, multi-user support, and OIDC/LDAP auth — especially if you run a reverse proxy with SSO.

alternatives.name: Tandoor Recipes
alternatives.text: Mealie if you want simpler setup, better mobile UX, and native OIDC; Tandoor if you want more granular permissions, advanced search (trigram), and AI-assisted features.

alternatives.name: RecipeSage
alternatives.text: Mealie if you want a single-container deploy with built-in auth providers; RecipeSage if you want Paprika import compatibility, offline PWA, or collaborative sharing with external users.

entries.name: Tandoor Recipes
prose: Django-based recipe manager built for households. Manage recipes, plan meals, build shopping lists, and organize cookbooks. Powerful search with PostgreSQL trigram similarity. Supports import from many other recipe managers. AI features for image recognition, step sorting, and nutrition lookup.
entries.pick: you want a power-user recipe manager with advanced search, fine-grained permissions for households, AI integrations, and don't mind running PostgreSQL alongside it.

alternatives.name: Mealie
alternatives.text: Tandoor if you need granular space/user permissions, trigram search, or AI-assisted recipe handling; Mealie if you prefer simpler setup and native OIDC.

alternatives.name: RecipeSage
alternatives.text: Tandoor if you want richer household permissions, advanced search, and Django admin flexibility; RecipeSage if you want offline PWA, real-time collaboration, or Paprika-format import.

entries.name: RecipeSage
prose: Collaborative recipe keeper, meal planner, and shopping list organizer delivered as a PWA. Imports from URL, image, PDF, or text. Supports Paprika, Pepperplate, Living Cookbook, Recipe Keeper, CopyMeThat, and CSV import formats. Works offline and syncs across devices. AI cooking assistant, nutrition tracking, recipe scaling with unit conversion.
entries.pick: you're migrating from Paprika or another commercial recipe app and want full import compatibility, offline-first PWA experience, and real-time collaboration on meal plans and shopping lists.

alternatives.name: Mealie
alternatives.text: RecipeSage if you need Paprika/Pepperplate import, offline PWA, or collaborative sharing with family who won't use your SSO; Mealie if you want simpler deploy, OIDC/LDAP auth, and a more traditional server-rendered feel.

alternatives.name: Tandoor Recipes
alternatives.text: RecipeSage if you want offline capability, broader import format support, or a PWA that feels native on mobile; Tandoor if you want Django power-user features, AI image recognition, or household permission spaces.

categories.label: Search
categories.description: Search engines, full-text search, and metasearch aggregators

entries.name: Meilisearch

fields.Auth: API key (master key → generates search/admin keys)

prose: Lightning-fast, typo-tolerant full-text search engine written in Rust. Sub-50ms queries out of the box with zero configuration. RESTful API, faceted search, filtering, sorting, multi-tenancy via tenant tokens, and automatic language detection.
entries.pick: you want instant search with typo tolerance, minimal resource usage, and the simplest possible setup — ideal for app-embedded search (docs sites, e-commerce, internal tools).

alternatives.name: Typesense
alternatives.text: Both are lightweight and developer-friendly. Meilisearch has simpler defaults and broader language support; Typesense has geosearch and more tuning knobs.

alternatives.name: Elasticsearch/OpenSearch
alternatives.text: Meilisearch for instant app search with minimal ops; Elasticsearch for log analytics, complex aggregations, or petabyte scale.

alternatives.name: SearXNG
alternatives.text: Different purpose. Meilisearch indexes your data; SearXNG aggregates external search engines.

entries.name: SearXNG

fields.Auth: none built-in (restrict access via reverse proxy or network)

prose: Privacy-respecting metasearch engine that aggregates results from 70+ search engines (Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, etc.) without tracking. Supports web, images, news, videos, science, files, music, and more. Configurable engines, bangs, and result formats.
entries.pick: you want a private, self-hosted search portal that queries multiple engines without leaking your searches to any single provider.

alternatives.name: Meilisearch/Typesense
alternatives.text: Different purpose. SearXNG queries the public internet; Meilisearch/Typesense index your own data.

alternatives.name: Elasticsearch/OpenSearch
alternatives.text: SearXNG is a search frontend/aggregator with zero indexing; Elasticsearch is a search backend that indexes data you feed it.

entries.name: Typesense
prose: Search-as-you-type engine built in C++ with an emphasis on low latency and developer experience. In-memory index for single-digit millisecond responses. Supports faceting, filtering, geosearch, synonyms, curation, and high-availability clustering.
entries.pick: you need sub-5ms search-as-you-type with geosearch, HA clustering, or fine-grained API key scoping — and you're comfortable with slightly more explicit schema configuration.

alternatives.name: Meilisearch
alternatives.text: Typesense has geosearch, joins, vector search, and more explicit schema control. Meilisearch has simpler setup, better typo handling, and broader default language support.

alternatives.name: Elasticsearch/OpenSearch
alternatives.text: Typesense for fast app search with minimal ops; Elasticsearch when you need log aggregation, complex query DSL, or multi-TB indexes.

alternatives.name: SearXNG
alternatives.text: Different purpose. Typesense indexes your data; SearXNG queries external engines.

entries.name: Elasticsearch / OpenSearch
prose: Distributed search and analytics engine for structured and unstructured data. Full-text search, log analytics, APM, vector/kNN search, and complex aggregations at scale. OpenSearch is the community-driven Apache-2.0 fork after Elastic's license change. Pairs with Kibana (Elastic) or OpenSearch Dashboards for visualization.

**OpenSearch vs Elasticsearch** — Feature-near-identical. Choose OpenSearch for Apache-2.0 licensing and community governance; Elasticsearch for tighter Kibana integration and faster feature releases from Elastic.
entries.pick: you need distributed full-text search at scale, log/event analytics (ELK/EFK stack), complex aggregations, or a mature ecosystem with extensive plugins and integrations.

alternatives.name: Meilisearch/Typesense
alternatives.text: Elasticsearch for analytics, logs, and complex queries at scale; Meilisearch/Typesense for lightweight instant app search with less operational overhead.

alternatives.name: SearXNG
alternatives.text: Different purpose. Elasticsearch indexes and analyzes your data; SearXNG is a privacy frontend for public search engines.

categories.label: Security & Identity
categories.description: Authentication, identity providers, SSO, password managers, and secrets management

entries.name: Authentik
prose: Full identity provider with flow-based authentication, application proxy, LDAP outpost, and user management. Beautiful admin UI.
entries.pick: you want a modern IdP with visual flow builder, built-in forward-auth proxy, and don't mind the resource usage.

alternatives.name: Keycloak
alternatives.text: Authentik for better UX and built-in proxy; Keycloak for enterprise maturity and broader protocol support.

alternatives.name: Authelia
alternatives.text: Authentik is a full IdP; Authelia is just a forward-auth proxy. Use Authentik if you want SSO for all your apps.

entries.name: Keycloak

fields.Auth: OIDC/OAuth2/SAML provider, LDAP federation, social login

prose: Enterprise-grade IdP by Red Hat. Battle-tested, massive protocol support, but steeper learning curve and heavier footprint.
entries.pick: you need enterprise-grade IdP with full SAML support, user federation, and don't mind Java-level resource usage.

alternatives.name: Authentik
alternatives.text: Keycloak for protocol depth and enterprise track record; Authentik for better DX and integrated proxy.

entries.name: Authelia

fields.Auth: forward-auth proxy (works with Nginx, Traefik, Caddy)

prose: Lightweight authentication and authorization server providing 2FA and SSO via forward-auth headers. Not a full IdP — it sits in front of your reverse proxy.
entries.pick: you just want "add login to any app behind your reverse proxy" without running a full IdP. Extremely lightweight.

alternatives.name: Authentik/Keycloak
alternatives.text: Authelia is not an IdP. It adds auth to apps that don't have it via reverse proxy headers. Use a full IdP if your apps support OIDC natively.

entries.name: Vaultwarden
prose: Lightweight Bitwarden-compatible server written in Rust. Works with all official Bitwarden clients and browser extensions. Unlocks premium features (TOTP, attachments, org vaults) for free.
entries.pick: you want self-hosted password management with Bitwarden's excellent clients but without the official server's heavy .NET stack.

alternatives.name: Bitwarden official
alternatives.text: Vaultwarden for lightweight self-hosting on a homelab; official Bitwarden server if you need enterprise compliance or support contracts.

categories.label: Tasks & Projects
categories.description: Task management, project tracking, kanban boards, and team collaboration

entries.name: Vikunja
prose: A full-featured to-do and project management app with lists, kanban, gantt charts, calendars, and reminders. Single Go binary with a Vue.js frontend — fast, low-resource, and easy to deploy. Supports CalDAV sync, file attachments, labels, priorities, assignees, and recurring tasks.
entries.pick: you want a personal or small-team task manager that covers to-dos, lists, and light project management without the weight of a full PM suite.

alternatives.name: Plane
alternatives.text: Vikunja is lighter and more personal-productivity focused (Todoist/Wunderlist replacement). Plane targets teams doing sprint planning and issue tracking (Jira replacement).

alternatives.name: Huly
alternatives.text: Vikunja is simpler and resource-friendly. Huly bundles docs, chat, and HR alongside task management. Choose Vikunja if you only need tasks.

alternatives.name: Kanboard
alternatives.text: Both are lightweight, but Vikunja has a modern UI, mobile apps, caldav, and more task features. Kanboard is simpler and pure kanban.

entries.name: Plane
prose: Open-source project management tool built as a Jira/Linear alternative. Issues, cycles (sprints), modules, views, pages (docs), and a beautiful UI. Supports custom workflows, bulk operations, analytics dashboards, and intake/triage flows.
entries.pick: you want a modern, team-oriented issue tracker with sprint planning, roadmaps, and a Linear-like UX — and you have the resources to run it.

alternatives.name: Vikunja
alternatives.text: Plane is heavier but purpose-built for team engineering workflows (sprints, modules, roadmaps). Vikunja is better for personal task management.

alternatives.name: Huly
alternatives.text: Both target teams, but Plane focuses on project/issue tracking while Huly bundles chat, docs, and HR. Plane has a more polished issue-tracking UX.

alternatives.name: Kanboard
alternatives.text: Plane is a full PM suite; Kanboard is a minimal kanban board. Plane when you need sprints and analytics; Kanboard when you want simplicity.

entries.name: Huly

fields.Resource: heavy (~1.5GB+; MongoDB + MinIO + Elastic + multiple services)

prose: All-in-one project management platform combining issues, documents, chat, HR, and time tracking. Real-time collaborative editing, Slack-like communication, and a polished UI. Aims to replace Linear + Notion + Slack in one self-hosted package.
entries.pick: you want a single platform for project management, team chat, and documentation — and you have the resources to run a larger stack.

alternatives.name: Vikunja
alternatives.text: Huly is far heavier and team-focused. Vikunja is ideal for personal to-dos and light project work without the overhead.

alternatives.name: Plane
alternatives.text: Huly bundles more (chat, docs, HR); Plane has a more focused and polished issue-tracking experience. Choose Plane for engineering PM, Huly if you want fewer separate tools.

alternatives.name: Kanboard
alternatives.text: Completely different weight classes. Kanboard for minimal kanban; Huly for teams wanting an integrated workspace.

entries.name: Kanboard

fields.Auth: built-in, LDAP, OIDC (via plugin), reverse proxy auth

prose: Minimalist kanban board focused on simplicity. No bloat — drag-and-drop tasks across columns, swimlanes, subtasks, time tracking, and analytics. Plugin system for extending functionality. Works great on low-powered hardware.
entries.pick: you want a dead-simple, no-frills kanban board with the smallest footprint and easy maintenance.

alternatives.name: Vikunja
alternatives.text: Kanboard is purer kanban with a more spartan UI. Vikunja has a modern interface, multiple views (list/kanban/gantt/calendar), and mobile apps.

alternatives.name: Plane
alternatives.text: Kanboard is minimal and personal; Plane is a full team PM suite. Kanboard if you just need cards on a board; Plane for sprint planning and roadmaps.

alternatives.name: Huly
alternatives.text: Kanboard for solo lightweight kanban; Huly for teams wanting an integrated all-in-one platform.

categories.label: Video Surveillance
categories.description: NVR, camera management, motion detection, and AI-powered monitoring

entries.name: Frigate

fields.Resource: heavy (~1GB idle; AI accelerator strongly recommended — Coral TPU or GPU)

prose: AI-powered NVR with realtime local object detection for IP cameras. Uses TensorFlow/OpenVINO/ONNX for detection, supports Google Coral TPU and various GPU accelerators. Tight Home Assistant integration via MQTT and a custom component. Features include 24/7 recording, motion-triggered object detection, zone-based alerts, RTSP re-streaming, WebRTC live view, and a review workflow for events.
entries.pick: you want the best-in-class AI object detection NVR, use Home Assistant, or have a Coral TPU / GPU available for inference. The modern UI, active community, and detection accuracy make it the top choice for homelabbers.

alternatives.name: ZoneMinder
alternatives.text: Frigate if you want modern AI detection, better UX, and Home Assistant integration; ZoneMinder if you need a traditional CCTV platform with decades of maturity, PTZ control, or zone-based legacy motion detection.

alternatives.name: Viseron
alternatives.text: Frigate if you want the larger community, better docs, polished UI, and Home Assistant support; Viseron if you want face recognition built-in or prefer a more modular/plugin architecture.

alternatives.name: Shinobi
alternatives.text: Frigate if you want AI detection and modern architecture; Shinobi if you need multi-tenant accounts, browser-based management for many cameras, or don't need AI.

entries.name: ZoneMinder
prose: Traditional open-source CCTV software with 20+ years of development. Supports IP, USB, and analog cameras. Features include zone-based motion detection, PTZ control, event recording, email/SMS alerts, multi-user access control, and an API. Can be extended with machine learning via the Event Notification Server (zmeventnotification) for object/face detection.
entries.pick: you want a battle-tested, feature-complete CCTV platform with granular zone configuration, PTZ support, and don't mind the legacy UI. Good for large camera counts with traditional motion detection requirements.

alternatives.name: Frigate
alternatives.text: ZoneMinder if you want PTZ control, traditional zone-based motion detection, or need the maturity of a 20-year-old project; Frigate if you want modern AI detection, better UX, and lower-latency live views.

alternatives.name: Viseron
alternatives.text: ZoneMinder if you need traditional CCTV features (PTZ, multi-user); Viseron if you want a more modern AI-first approach without the legacy baggage.

alternatives.name: Shinobi
alternatives.text: ZoneMinder if you want GPL licensing and proven stability; Shinobi if you prefer a modern Node.js stack and multi-tenant architecture.

entries.name: Viseron

fields.Resource: heavy (~1GB; GPU recommended for AI — supports CUDA, VAAPI, EdgeTPU, Hailo)

prose: Self-hosted, local-only NVR with AI computer vision. Features object detection, motion detection, face recognition, license plate recognition, and post-processing. Modular component architecture supports multiple detection backends (DeepStack, CodeProject.AI, YOLO, EdgeTPU, Hailo). Includes a web UI with live views and event browsing.
entries.pick: you want built-in face recognition or license plate detection, prefer a modular plugin architecture, or want to run multiple AI backends simultaneously. Good alternative to Frigate if you don't use Home Assistant.

alternatives.name: Frigate
alternatives.text: Viseron if you want native face recognition, don't use Home Assistant, or prefer its plugin system; Frigate if you want larger community, better docs, more polished UI, and tighter HA integration.

alternatives.name: ZoneMinder
alternatives.text: Viseron if you want modern AI without legacy baggage; ZoneMinder if you need PTZ, multi-user, or traditional CCTV features.

alternatives.name: Shinobi
alternatives.text: Viseron if you want AI-first with face/plate recognition; Shinobi if you need multi-tenant management or a simpler non-AI setup.

entries.name: Shinobi
prose: Open-source CCTV platform written in Node.js. Designed for multi-account/multi-tenant use with WebSocket-based streaming. Supports 6000+ camera models via ONVIF/RTSP/MJPEG. Features include motion detection, recording schedules, two-factor auth, plugin system for object detection (via external plugins), and a developer-friendly API.
entries.pick: you need multi-tenant camera management (separate accounts per user/site), want a modern Node.js stack, or need an API-first platform for integration. Good for small businesses managing cameras across multiple locations.

alternatives.name: Frigate
alternatives.text: Shinobi if you need multi-tenant accounts or don't need AI; Frigate if you want object detection, Home Assistant integration, and active development.

alternatives.name: ZoneMinder
alternatives.text: Shinobi if you want modern architecture, multi-tenant, and WebSocket streaming; ZoneMinder if you want GPL licensing, PTZ control, and proven long-term stability.

alternatives.name: Viseron
alternatives.text: Shinobi if you need multi-user accounts and simpler non-AI recording; Viseron if you want native AI detection and face recognition.

categories.label: VPN & Remote Access
categories.description: VPN servers, mesh networking, remote desktop, and tunneling

entries.name: WireGuard

fields.Resource: minimal (~10MB kernel module; ~50MB with GUI wrapper)

prose: Extremely fast, modern VPN protocol built into the Linux kernel. Minimal attack surface (~4000 lines of code), cryptographically sound (Noise protocol framework), and outperforms IPsec/OpenVPN on throughput and latency.
entries.pick: you want raw VPN performance with minimal overhead, already manage your own key distribution, or need a single point-to-point or hub-and-spoke tunnel without extra dependencies.

alternatives.name: Tailscale/Headscale
alternatives.text: WireGuard for raw protocol control and zero dependencies; Tailscale/Headscale for automatic key exchange, NAT traversal, and mesh topology.

alternatives.name: NetBird
alternatives.text: WireGuard for simplicity and kernel-level speed; NetBird for managed mesh with SSO and ACLs on top of WireGuard.

alternatives.name: OpenVPN
alternatives.text: WireGuard for speed, simplicity, and modern crypto; OpenVPN for legacy compatibility and TCP fallback.

entries.name: Tailscale / Headscale

fields.Auth: SSO via identity provider (Tailscale SaaS); OIDC (Headscale)

prose: Mesh VPN built on WireGuard that handles key exchange, NAT traversal (DERP relays), and peer discovery automatically. Tailscale is the hosted SaaS; Headscale is the self-hosted, open-source control server implementing the Tailscale coordination protocol.
entries.pick: you want zero-config mesh networking across NATs with automatic peer discovery, MagicDNS, and ACLs — especially if you want to self-host the control plane (Headscale).

alternatives.name: WireGuard
alternatives.text: Tailscale/Headscale for automatic mesh topology, NAT traversal, and SSO; raw WireGuard for maximum control and no coordination server.

alternatives.name: NetBird
alternatives.text: Tailscale/Headscale for maturity and ecosystem (Funnel, Serve, exit nodes); NetBird for native OIDC integration, network policies, and self-hosted-first design.

alternatives.name: Nebula
alternatives.text: Tailscale/Headscale for ease of setup and richer features; Nebula for certificate-based auth and Slack-backed pedigree.

entries.name: NetBird

fields.Auth: OIDC / SSO (Authentik, Keycloak, Zitadel, Auth0, Google, etc.)

prose: Mesh networking platform that combines WireGuard tunnels with SSO-based identity, network policies (ACLs, routes, DNS), and NAT traversal. Self-hosted-first architecture with a management UI for peer groups, access control, and posture checks.
entries.pick: you want a self-hosted mesh VPN with first-class SSO integration (e.g., Authentik), granular network policies, and a management UI — especially in a homelab already running an IdP.

alternatives.name: Tailscale/Headscale
alternatives.text: NetBird for native self-hosted design with rich ACLs and SSO from day one; Tailscale/Headscale for maturity, larger community, and extra features (Funnel, exit nodes).

alternatives.name: WireGuard
alternatives.text: NetBird for managed mesh with identity-based access; WireGuard for raw tunnel performance with manual key management.

alternatives.name: ZeroTier
alternatives.text: NetBird for WireGuard-based speed and OIDC auth; ZeroTier for layer-2 virtual networking and longer track record.

entries.name: Guacamole

fields.Resource: medium (~500MB; Java client + C daemon + DB)
fields.Auth: built-in (database) + OIDC, LDAP, SAML, TOTP, header auth

prose: Clientless remote desktop gateway — access RDP, VNC, SSH, Telnet, and Kubernetes terminals through a web browser with no plugins or client software required. Supports session recording, file transfer, and multi-factor auth.
entries.pick: you want browser-based remote access to desktops and servers without installing client software — ideal for accessing Windows machines, jumpboxes, or lab hosts from any device.

alternatives.name: RustDesk
alternatives.text: Guacamole for browser-based access to existing RDP/VNC/SSH; RustDesk for peer-to-peer remote desktop with its own client.

alternatives.name: MeshCentral
alternatives.text: Guacamole for protocol-gateway simplicity (RDP/VNC/SSH via browser); MeshCentral for full remote management suite with agents, file transfer, and device inventory.

alternatives.name: Apache NiFi + SSH
alternatives.text: Guacamole for interactive GUI/terminal sessions; direct SSH/RDP for scripted access without a web layer.
